title: {{NAME}} and the Fairy Robot Festival
moral: Everyone belongs, no matter how different they seem.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a shimmery sky-blue royal tunic with tiny fairy wings printed all over it, silver trousers, sky-blue boots with little silver buttons, and a small silver crown on his head — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content: {{NAME}} walked into the Fairy Festival garden. The garden had lanterns in every colour. Fairies flew all around dropping gold sparkles. A princess in a bright pink dress was handing out flowers. Then a small silver robot walked in through the gate. The robot looked around with big hopeful eyes. Nobody had invited a robot before.

pages.content: The robot said his name was Pip. Some fairies flew away from Pip. They had never seen a robot at the festival. Pip's eyes dimmed. He turned to go back through the gate. {{NAME}} looked at the princess. She had a kind face. Together they ran to Pip. "Please stay," said {{NAME}}. "You are welcome here."

pages.content: Pip smiled again. His eyes glowed happy blue. He showed everyone his special trick. He could spin his arms very fast and blow soft golden bubbles into the air. The fairies flew through the bubbles and they turned into tiny stars. Everyone clapped and laughed. The festival had never been so magical.

Pip's chest glowed warm orange with happiness. Everyone belongs, no matter how different they seem. {{NAME}} felt his heart feel big and full.

pages.content: When the festival ended, they all sat under a glowing lantern tree. The fairies settled on the branches above. Pip hummed a soft sleepy tune. Everyone belongs, no matter how different they seem. {{NAME}} felt cosy and warm and very sleepy. He closed his eyes slowly. He wondered what new trick Pip might show them all next time.
